verdict.rationale: Solid's own README states that when state changes, only the code that depends on it reruns. It backs this with signals (count/setCount), automatic dependency tracking, derived state, and fine-grained DOM updates instead of a virtual DOM. Community users independently confirm granular, fine-grained updates in real projects. Missing for 10: tooling or lint to catch the documented pitfall where destructuring props or stores silently loses reactivity, and evidence deeper than README-level documentation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can declare reactive state and have only the dependent UI code re-run when it changes

citations.quote: Declare your state and use it throughout your app, and when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.
Automatic dependency tracking: accessing your reactive state subscribes to it
Create a piece of reactive state, giving us an accessor, count(), and a setter, setCount()
Instead of using a Virtual DOM, it compiles its templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactions.
Solid realizes the full potential of fine-grained reactive updates
